system.name: Social-Evol (agent cognitive architecture MoRE)
system.one_liner: An LLM-agent simulation of a prehistoric hunter-gatherer society, with agents of four moral types, used to study how morality evolves.

content.variant_note: one framed agent cognitive architecture on top, an illustrated environment of coordination and action rounds below, two labelled long arrows between them and an analysis assistant agent at the lower left
content.argues: Agents with different moral types that perceive, remember, reflect and plan can be placed in a simulated society whose rounds and dynamics are explicit, and the results are analysed by an assistant agent.
content.subject: the agent cognitive architecture MoRE, the Environment with its rounds and dynamics, and the Simulation Analysis Assistant Agent

elements.name: Agent Cognitive Architecture (MoRE)
elements.role: the cognitive modules of one agent: moral values, perception, memory, reflection and action planning
elements.drawn_as: large black-framed band with a blue bold title and a red italic MoRE, holding the module panels

elements.name: Moral Types
elements.role: prescribes the agent's moral type based on expanding circles of concern
elements.drawn_as: panel with a yellow header holding four nested rounded cards, each with a one-sentence rule and a cartoon character

elements.name: Universal, Reciprocal, Kin-focused and Selfish Moral Agents
elements.role: the four moral types: help anyone and harm no one even when exploited; help anyone as long as they treat back; help only kin; care for no one, even family, but reproduce more
elements.drawn_as: nested rounded cards, outer red (Universal), gold (Reciprocal), green (Kin-focused), innermost blue (Selfish)

elements.name: Reflection
elements.role: self-check before execution for consistency with facts and the moral type
elements.drawn_as: lavender-headed bar with four numbered questions, e.g. Am I faithful to my moral type?

elements.name: Perception
elements.role: processes environmental information: plants and prey status, agent status, recent steps
elements.drawn_as: panel with a green header and three rounded green cards (Plants & Prey, Agent Status, Recent N Steps Activities)

elements.name: Immediate Action Plan
elements.role: forms the short-term plan and chooses the current action from the action space
elements.drawn_as: blue-headed frame with Short-term Action Planning on top, a down arrow, and Current Action Choice below

elements.name: Entity-based Memory, Judgement and Disposition Processing
elements.role: updates memory and judgements per entity: reproduction and family, agents, hunting and prey
elements.drawn_as: peach-headed frame holding three peach cards (Reproduction Module, Agent-specific Module, Hunting Module) with italic field lines and ellipses

elements.name: Environment
elements.role: the simulated world that follows defined temporal dynamics and alternates coordination and action rounds with the agents
elements.drawn_as: black-framed band with a blue bold title, two illustrated scenes and a loop arrow between them

elements.name: Multi Coordination Round
elements.role: round in which agents coordinate: Allocate and Communicate
elements.drawn_as: left illustrated scene with a blue label and white outlined verbs on the picture

elements.name: Action Round
elements.role: round in which agents act: Reproduce, Fight, Rob, Collect, Hunt
elements.drawn_as: right illustrated scene with a green label and white outlined verbs on the picture

elements.name: Temporal Dynamics
elements.role: world changes over time: HP drops and plants and prey respawn
elements.drawn_as: caption at the right of the Environment with a heart marked -1 beside a caveman and a plant and deer pair

elements.name: Simulation Analysis Assistant Agent
elements.role: tool that automatically analyses simulation results: experiment reports and interactive Q&A
elements.drawn_as: black-framed box with a blue bold title and bullet lists (Statistics, Figures/Tables, Code Copilot)

elements.name: Simulation Results
elements.role: what the Environment hands to the assistant: agent logs, checkpoints and more
elements.drawn_as: italic caption with bullets beside a large pale block arrow pointing left

elements.name: Social-Evol
elements.role: names the framework and its environment
elements.drawn_as: very large bold italic title at the left of the Environment band

encoding.shape_means: nested rounded cards = circles of concern; module card with bold header and italic field lines = a module's fields; illustrated scene = one kind of round
encoding.marker_means: numbers 1 to 4 = reflection checks; ellipsis = more fields or more agents

lessons.what_to_learn: Pair an agent's cognitive architecture, drawn as module cards with a few field lines, with an illustrated environment whose round types are written on the scene, and join them with two captioned arrows (action out, dynamics in). Nested rounded cards draw any ordered scope, such as circles of concern.
lessons.suits: LLM agent simulations or social-science papers in which an agent architecture meets a simulated world with distinct round types and an analysis tool.

evidence: SOCIAL-EVOL (Fig. 1) is a text-based prehistoric hunter-gatherer society with resource constraints, social dynamics, and environmental challenges
a moral value module prescribing moral types based on expanding circles of concern
Before execution, agents perform self-reflection to verify consistency with observed facts and moral dispositions.

summary: Social-Evol is an LLM-based agent simulation of a prehistoric hunter-gatherer society, built to study why morality evolves. Figure 1 draws the whole framework. The top band is the Agent Cognitive Architecture (MoRE): a Moral Types panel of four nested cards (universal, reciprocal, kin-focused, selfish) standing for expanding circles of concern, a Reflection checklist, a Perception panel, an Immediate Action Plan and entity-based memory modules. Two long arrows join it to the Environment below, shown as two illustrated scenes with action verbs overlaid, one for the multi-coordination round and one for the action round, plus temporal dynamics such as HP drops and respawning. A Simulation Analysis Assistant Agent box receives the simulation results.
summary_zh: Social-Evol 用 LLM 智能体模拟史前采集狩猎社会，研究道德为何演化。图一上方是认知架构 MoRE（四种嵌套的道德类型、反思、感知、行动规划与记忆模块），下方是插画环境和模拟分析助手智能体，之间用带标注的长箭头相连。
notes: Prior kinds kept in order (actor-interaction, model-anatomy); the variant is single-agent-loop rather than multi-agent-organization because one agent architecture is drawn against the Environment, although the text says the society holds several agents. Origins of the cartoon characters and the scenes are not stated; they look illustrated or AI-generated. The direction of the Reflection to memory arrow follows the drawing's small arrowheads and is partly a reading of tiny arrow marks.
